name: The ten grounds of the Madhyamakāvatāra

stages.name: Before the grounds: compassion, non-dual understanding and the awakening mind
stages.description: The ordinary bodhisattva cultivates compassion, the awakening mind and non-dual understanding (MA 1.1–2); hearing emptiness with joy marks a fit vessel (MA 6.4–5).

stages.name: Pramuditā
stages.description: The first ground, on which the perfection of giving (dāna) predominates. Emptiness is seen directly for the first time; the bodhisattva rejoices, having become a child of the Victors.

stages.name: Vimalā
stages.description: The second ground, on which the perfection of discipline (śīla) predominates.

stages.name: Prabhākarī
stages.description: The third ground, on which the perfection of patience (kṣānti) predominates.

stages.name: Arciṣmatī
stages.description: The fourth ground, on which the perfection of vigour (vīrya) predominates.

stages.name: Sudurjayā
stages.description: The fifth ground, on which the perfection of meditation (dhyāna) predominates.

stages.name: Abhimukhī
stages.description: The sixth ground, on which the perfection of wisdom (prajñā) predominates. Here the long exposition of emptiness (MA 6) is given; the bodhisattva can enter cessation.

stages.name: Dūraṃgamā
stages.description: The seventh ground, on which the perfection of method (upāya) predominates.

stages.name: Acalā
stages.description: The eighth ground, on which the perfection of aspiration (praṇidhāna) predominates. The bodhisattva is irreversible and no longer moved by conceptual effort.

stages.name: Sādhumatī
stages.description: The ninth ground, on which the perfection of power (bala) predominates.

stages.name: Dharmameghā
stages.description: The tenth ground, on which the perfection of knowledge (jñāna) predominates.

stages.name: The Buddha ground
stages.description: The qualities of the grounds culminate in buddhahood, with the bodies and activity of a Buddha, who remains for beings without abiding in nirvāṇa.

notes: Ground names confirmed for grounds 1, 4 and 5 in the local e-text of the bhāṣya; the others and their pairing with the ten perfections follow the Daśabhūmika tradition (pth:ten-bhumis).

name: The sequence of the Bodhicaryāvatāra

stages.name: Praise of the awakening mind
stages.description: Seeing the benefits of the awakening mind and resolving to hold it.

stages.name: Worship and confession
stages.description: Offering, refuge and confession of faults before the Buddhas.

stages.name: Adopting the awakening mind
stages.description: Rejoicing, requesting, dedicating, and generating the awakening mind with the vow.

stages.name: Conscientiousness
stages.description: Guarding the awakening mind and vow; fighting the afflictions.

stages.name: Guarding introspection
stages.description: Guarding the mind with mindfulness and introspection; the bodhisattva's conduct.

stages.name: Patience
stages.description: Overcoming anger by reflection.

stages.name: Vigour
stages.description: Delight in the good; overcoming laziness.

stages.name: Meditation
stages.description: Solitude, calm, and the equalizing and exchanging of self and other.

stages.name: Wisdom
stages.description: The two truths, the refutation of realists, mind-only and the self, and meditation on emptiness till the mind rests without object.

stages.name: Dedication
stages.description: Dedicating the merit to all beings and resolving to remain for them as long as space endures.

notes: A sequence of practice chapters rather than a staged map of attainment; the dedication chapter is left unbanded.

stages.name: Compassion
stages.description: Compassion is cultivated first as the root of all Buddha qualities.

stages.name: The awakening mind
stages.description: Aspiring and engaging bodhicitta.

stages.name: Practice of method: the perfections
stages.description: Giving and the other perfections, joined with wisdom.

stages.name: Hearing and reflection
stages.description: Wisdom from hearing grasps scripture; wisdom from reflection discerns definitive from provisional meaning.

stages.name: Calm abiding
stages.description: The nine stages of settling the mind, removing the six faults by the eight remedies.

stages.name: Insight through correct analysis
stages.description: Analysing the self and dharmas until no own-nature is found; calm and insight balanced.

stages.name: Non-conceptual wisdom
stages.description: When no dharma is found arisen in the three times, the yogin enters non-conceptual wisdom, the first direct seeing (the first ground).

stages.name: Cultivation through the grounds
stages.description: The path of cultivation through the ten grounds.

stages.name: Buddhahood and non-abiding nirvāṇa
stages.description: Omniscience; by great compassion the Buddha does not abide in nirvāṇa but acts for the world.

stages.name: The dharma of higher status
stages.description: Through faith: the ten virtuous paths, non-drinking, right livelihood, non-harm, giving, honouring the honourable and love, leading to happiness in good rebirths.

stages.name: The dharma of definite goodness
stages.description: Through wisdom: seeing that 'I' and 'mine' are false and passing beyond existence and non-existence, which is liberation.

stages.name: The bodhisattva's collections and grounds
stages.description: The collections of merit and wisdom and the ten grounds leading to the two bodies of a Buddha.

stages.name: Buddhahood
stages.description: The form bodies from merit and the truth body from wisdom.

stages.name: Turning away from demerit
stages.description: First, turning from non-virtue.

stages.name: Turning away from self
stages.description: In the middle, turning from grasping at a self.

stages.name: Turning away from everything
stages.description: Finally, turning from all views (commentary).

name: The ladder of views (Madhyamakālaṃkāra 92–93)

stages.name: Relying on mind-only
stages.description: Understanding that external objects do not exist.

stages.name: Relying on the Madhyamaka
stages.description: Understanding that even mind is utterly without self.

stages.name: Riding the two chariots
stages.description: Holding the reins of reasoning over both systems, one is a true Mahāyānist.

notes: A ladder of doctrinal understanding rather than a meditative map; left unbanded.
